title: ModSec-Learn: Boosting ModSecurity with Machine Learning
abstract: arXiv:2406.13547v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: ModSecurity is widely recognized as the standard open-source Web Application Firewall (WAF), maintained by the OWASP Foundation. It detects malicious requests by matching them against the Core Rule Set (CRS), identifying well-known attack patterns. Each rule is manually assigned a weight based on the severity of the corresponding attack, and a request is blocked if the sum of the weights of matched rules exceeds a given threshold. However, we argue that this strategy is largely ineffective against web attacks, as detection is only based on heuristics and not customized on the application to protect. translated_abstract: ModSecurity被广泛认为是标准的开源Web应用防火墙（WAF），由OWASP基金会维护。它通过将请求与核心规则集（CRS）进行匹配来检测恶意请求，从而识别已知的攻击模式。每条规则根据相应攻击的严重程度被手动分配一个权重，当匹配规则的权重之和超过给定阈值时，请求就会被拦截。然而，我们认为这种策略对Web攻击的防御效果很大程度上是无效的，因为检测仅基于启发式方法，而未针对需要保护的应用程序进行定制。在这项工作中，我们通过提出一种以CRS规则作为输入特征的机器学习模型来解决这一问题。通过训练，ModSec-Learn能够调整每条CRS规则对预测结果的贡献，从而使严重性级别适应于需要保护的Web应用程序。我们的实验表明，ModSec-Learn取得了显著的（检测效果提升）。
tldr: 提出ModSec-Learn，一种以ModSecurity核心规则集（CRS）规则作为输入特征的机器学习模型，通过训练自动调整各规则对预测的贡献，使WAF的检测严重性级别能够自适应地针对特定Web应用进行定制，从而显著提升对Web攻击的检测效果。
en_tdlr: ModSec-Learn is a machine learning model that uses ModSecurity's Core Rule Set (CRS) rules as input features, automatically tuning each rule's contribution to predictions through training, thereby adapting the severity levels to the specific web applications being protected and significantly improving detection of web attacks over the traditional heuristic threshold-based approach.
